units: <cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 32:2">Lev. R. s. 32</cite> (ref. to <he>ויקצף</he>, <cite ref="Deuteronomy 1:34">Deut. I, 34</cite>) <he>להם הוא ק׳ ולי מה אני ק׳ וכ׳</he> to them it appears as anger, but to myself what does anger mean? ‘I swore by my anger’ (<cite ref="Psalms 95:11">Ps. XCV, 11</cite>), I swear by my anger and reconsider; Yalk. ib. 657.

<cite ref="Esther Rabbah 4:8">Esth. R. to I, 18</cite> <he>כדאי הוא הבזיון … לק׳ שקצף וכ׳</he> the disrespect with which her (Vashti’s) father treated the vessels of the Temple is enough to deserve the wrath which he (Ahasverus) vented on her and put her to death.
<cite ref="Esther Rabbah 4:8">Ib.</cite> <he>כדי הק׳ לבזיון זה</he> the anger (of Ahasverus) corresponds to this contempt (shown by Vashti), v. <cite ref="S01819"><he>קְצִיפָה</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Esther Rabbah 4:8">Ib.</cite> to II, 21 <he>מה ק׳ היה שם</he> what cause was there for discontent? Sifra Sh’mini, Par. 1, ch. II (ref. to <cite ref="Leviticus 10:16">Lev. X, 16</cite>) <he>אף אהרן היה בק׳</he> Aaron, too, was included in the anger (of Moses). Pesik. Vattom., p. 130ᵇ <he>אין ק׳ הוא</he> (not <cite ref="S01835"><he>קצפין</he></cite>), v. <cite ref="S01819"><he>קְצִיפָה</he></cite>.
